input.question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick
input.ground_truth: Because it can. Moving from extreme temperatures one to another can weaken your immune system and that makes it easier for you to get sick. So while it won't directly make you sick to be out in the cold, going between temps is what will do it. Unless it's something like hypothermia. That can make you sick just from being out in the cold.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick

Answer:

response.prediction:
Sure! Here’s how you could explain it to a 5-year-old:

When you are out in really cold weather or you swim in cold water, your body gets very chilly. Sometimes, if you get too cold, it can make it easier for germs (tiny bugs that can make you sick) to sneak into your body and make you feel yucky. But actually, just being cold by itself doesn’t make you sick. It’s when you get too cold and maybe your body gets weak, that germs can make you sick more easily.

So, being cold doesn’t *directly* make you sick, but it can help germs make you sick if you’re not careful! That’s why grown-ups tell you to dress warmly and not stay out in the cold too long.
